main_result: Claims that every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex v with |N1+(v)| <= |N2+(v)|, where N2+ excludes v and N1+. This resolves Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture. Corollaries: weighted forms (via Seacrest's equivalences); a non-neighbour bound (some v with d+(v) <= |Z(v)| and n-1 >= 2d+(v)+d-(v)) when there is no directed triangle; a directed triangle when min in- and out-degree >= n/3; and n >= 3r+1 for r-regular digraphs of directed girth 4.
proof_strategy: Minimal counterexample D (min order, then min arcs). Lemma subset-deficit: by deleting arcs from S to E\T and tracking exact second out-neighbourhoods, each vertex's Q-increment of g is strictly less than |Q|, giving |F^2(S)\F(S)| < |F(S)\S| for proper S. Lemma blowup replaces each vertex by a transitive tournament, giving |U|+|F^2(U)| < 2|F(U)| for all proper nonempty U. Proposition no-concavity takes a compatible pair of families (P,Q) containing the diagonal, maximising |P|+|Q|+d, applies the strict inequality column-wise and row-wise, complements the second images to get families R, C with |R|+|C| > M+2d, and then prunes conflicts via Lemma pruning, a matching/König argument using generic rank (Lemma kernel-support) to bound deletions by |H|+q with |H| <= d. The contradiction is M+d < |P'|+|Q'|+d'. I checked each displayed inequality in these steps and found them consistent; the step I could not independently certify to the level of a published result is the simultaneous generic-rank choice in Lemma pruning. Unclear: whether the chosen coefficients realise all three rank conditions at one real point, which I reconstructed only by the product-of-nonzero-polynomials sketch.
hardest_part: The simultaneous coefficient choice in the proof of Lemma pruning: one real assignment must make L, N^T, all D^{p,i} (each at maximum support rank) and the matching minors nonzero at once, while the variables a_{pi} and b_{sj} are shared across many of these matrices. I could follow the polynomial-product argument, but the non-cancellation claims and the max-rank-on-support genericity are compressed, and I checked them only by reconstruction. The overall result also rests on this lemma, so I would not trust my verification of it as a substitute for a careful line-by-line check.

main_result: Every nonempty finite oriented graph D has a vertex v with |N1+(v)| <= |N2+(v)|, where N2+(v) is the set of vertices at exact directed distance two from v. This is Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture. Corollaries: weighted vertex forms (for every nonnegative weighting some vertex is good; some normalized weighting makes every vertex good), an arc-weighted form via Seacrest, and directed-cycle consequences (no directed triangle implies n-1 >= 2d+(v)+d-(v) for some v; min in- and out-degree >= n/3 forces a directed triangle; r-regular girth-4 digraphs have n >= 3r+1).
proof_strategy: Assume a counterexample and take one of minimum order and then minimum arc count. Arc deletion on the counterexample gives a strict deficit |F^2(S)\F(S)| < |F(S)\S| for every nonempty proper S, and blowing each vertex up into a transitive tournament turns this into |U|+|F^2(U)| < 2|F(U)| for all nonempty proper U (Proposition on counterexample reduction, Lemmas subset-deficit and blowup). An extremal argument then takes two compatible families of ordered pairs (maximizing |P|+|Q|+uncovered points), applies the strict inequalities to columns/rows and complements to get a larger combined objective, and restores compatibility with a pruning lemma. The pruning lemma bounds deletions by a König cover of an augmented bipartite graph, using a maximum-matching bound proved by rank arguments: a coefficient assignment makes rank L = l, rank N = t, and kernel lifts give dim ker A >= k, with the identity NL = AB and Lemma kernel-support supplying the key vanishing. I checked the chain of inequalities in each lemma and found no error, but the simultaneous coefficient choice in the pruning lemma is only sketched.
hardest_part: The pruning lemma (Lemma pruning and its rank proof). I reconstructed the chain |H| >= dim ker A + rank A >= k + rank(NL) >= k + l + t - |Z| and the kernel-lift independence argument, and they hold given the stated choices. However, the simultaneous choice of coefficients (rank L = l, rank N = t, maximal-rank D^{p,i} for every arrow, nonvanishing of all minors at one real point) is argued only by a short sketch of polynomial nonvanishing. Also the augmenting-path claim for alpha and beta is compressed. This is the step on which the whole extremal contradiction depends, and I would not trust my check of it without a careful independent reading. The statement is a strong, unusual result for an open conjecture, so an independent expert check of the whole argument is warranted.

main_result: Every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex v with |N_1^+(v)| <= |N_2^+(v)|, where N_1^+ is the out-neighbourhood and N_2^+ is the set of vertices at directed distance exactly two. This is Seymour's second neighbourhood conjecture. Corollaries give the vertex- and arc-weighted forms (via Seacrest's equivalences) and directed-cycle/degree consequences (non-neighbour counts, the one-third-degree triangle result, and a girth-four order bound for regular digraphs).
proof_strategy: Minimal-counterexample reduction: in a minimal counterexample, an arc-deletion argument (Lemma subset-deficit) gives |F^2(S)\F(S)| < |F(S)\S| for all nonempty proper S. A lexicographic blow-up by transitive tournaments (Lemma blowup) converts this into a strict inequality |U|+|F^2(U)| < 2|F(U)| for all nonempty proper U. Proposition no-concavity then maximises M+d over compatible pairs of coordinate-image families containing the diagonal, takes complements of second images to get two larger families that may conflict, and removes conflicts with a pruning lemma (Lemma pruning). Pruning is a König-type cover bound obtained from a matching bound in an augmented bipartite graph, proved with a generic-rank/kernel argument (Lemma kernel-support). The pruning cost is at most |H| + d', which yields a strictly larger objective and a contradiction. I checked each step of these chains and found them consistent; the weaker points are the generic-rank facts and cited results, which I did not re-derive.
hardest_part: The rank argument inside Lemma pruning: the simultaneous choice of coefficients (nonvanishing of the alpha and beta minors together with maximum-rank minors for each D^{p,i}), and the kernel-restriction step (conflict-kernel identity) that makes the lifts Bu^r independent. I verified the algebra line by line and it holds as far as I can tell, but it depends on generic-rank facts that the text asserts rather than proves, and on a shared-variable polynomial-nonvanishing argument. I also could not independently check the cited Seacrest statements, so the weighted corollary rests on citations.
